analysis.title: Purposefully higher rates to cool inflation
key_insights: The Fed delivered a third straight 75bp hike at the September 2022 FOMC, in line with market expectations, taking the Fed funds target range to 3.00%-3.25%. Policy rates are entering what Powell called the lowest level of what is restrictive.

The dot plot shifted up meaningfully. The 2022 median dot is 4.375% and every FOMC member except one expects rates above 4.00% by year-end. It was a close call with 4.125%, and one lower dot would have cut the median by 25bp.

A 4.375% year-end midpoint implies another 125bp of hikes, for example 75bp in November and 50bp in December. The market prices 70bp for the 2 November meeting and 116bp in total over the next two meetings.
The dots signal one more 25bp hike in 2023, with the median at 4.625% as the cycle peak. Cuts follow to 3.875% in 2024 and 2.875% in 2025. The longer-run dot is unchanged at 2.50%.

Market pricing of the terminal rate rose modestly to about 4.54% in March 2023, roughly in line with the dot plot. The market still prices a little over 30bp of cuts between March and December 2023, which CA-CIB sees as overly optimistic.

Front end rates jumped on the higher dots while long end rates fell on expectations that higher policy rates would weaken growth. The 2-10Y curve hit a new cycle trough of -52bp and CA-CIB expects further flattening as short dated rates keep rising.

The FOMC cut its growth forecasts sharply, with 2022 GDP at 0.2% vs 1.7% previously and 2023 at 1.2% vs 1.7%. CA-CIB thinks the 2023 number may still be too optimistic and that a soft landing may be difficult.

Unemployment projections rose to 4.4% in 2023 vs 3.9% in June and hold at 4.4% in 2024. The report notes this meets the Sahm rule threshold of a 0.5ppt rise, which typically signals recession. Powell declined to put odds on a recession.

Inflation projections were revised up slightly. Q4 2022 headline PCE is 5.4% (vs 5.2%) and core PCE 4.5% (vs 4.3%). Q4 2023 headline is 2.8% (vs 2.6%) and core 3.1% (vs 2.7%). Both measures return near target only by 2025.
Balance sheet runoff stays on autopilot, with the monthly cap doubled to USD95bn this month. Powell said the Fed is not considering MBS sales in the near term.
CA-CIB sees the employment report on 7 October and CPI on 13 October as the key data for sizing the next hike.

tension_points.bull_case: The market prices a little over 30bp of cuts between March and December 2023, expecting easing sooner than the dot plot indicates.
tension_points.bear_case: CA-CIB sees that pricing as overly optimistic, since the dots show a 4.625% peak in 2023 and the Fed pledges to hold rates in restrictive territory for some time.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The employment report on 7 October and CPI on 13 October are the key data points CA-CIB names for judging the size of the next hike.
